# actiplot

`actiplot` provides `ggplot2` visualizations for minute-level activity
data, including steps and activity counts. It works with the
standardized timestamp conventions used throughout the activerse.

## Example-data provenance

`acti_minute_data` is a processed minute-level recording drawn from the
[Figshare collection of upper-limb activity
data](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.4457855) from 20 myoelectric
prosthesis users and 20 anatomically intact adults. Please cite the
original data descriptor when using it: Chadwell A, Kenney L, Granat M,
Thies S, Galpin A, and Head J (2019), [*Upper limb activity of twenty
myoelectric prosthesis users and twenty healthy anatomically intact
adults*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-019-0211-6), *Scientific Data*
6, 199.

Core entry points:

- [`acti_plot_time()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/acti_plot_time.md)
  for a complete activity time series
- [`acti_plot_day()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/acti_plot_time.md)
  for time-of-day-aligned daily rows
- [`acti_plot_heatmap()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/acti_plot_time.md)
  for a date-by-time activity heat map

## Installation

You can install `actiplot` from GitHub with:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("jhuwit/actiplot")
```

## Quick start

``` r

activity <- acti_minute_data[seq_len(1440), ]

acti_plot_time(activity, counts, breaks = "4 hours")
```

![](reference/figures/README-example-1.png)

``` r

acti_plot_day(activity, counts, breaks = "4 hours")
```

![](reference/figures/README-example-2.png)

Daily facets can use a compact month-and-day label or baseline-relative
day numbers: `facet = "month-day"` and `facet = "day"`, respectively.

``` r

acti_plot_day(activity, counts, facet = "month-day")
```

![](reference/figures/README-day-facets-1.png)

``` r

acti_plot_day(activity, counts, facet = "day")
```

![](reference/figures/README-day-facets-2.png)

For a complete recording, `x_axis = "12 hours"` labels midnight and noon
with both the date and a 12-hour clock. Use `x_axis = "midnight"` when a
date-only label at midnight is preferred.

``` r

acti_plot_time(acti_minute_data, counts, x_axis = "12 hours")
```

![](reference/figures/README-time-axis-labels-1.png)

``` r

acti_plot_time(acti_minute_data, counts, x_axis = "midnight")
```

![](reference/figures/README-time-axis-labels-2.png)

``` r

acti_plot_day(acti_minute_data, counts, breaks = "4 hours")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-1-1.png)

# Package index

## All functions

- [`acti_minute_data`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/acti_minute_data.md)
  : Minute-level accelerometer counts
- [`acti_plot_actogram()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/acti_plot_actogram.md)
  : Plot an activity actogram
- [`acti_plot_minute_profile()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/acti_plot_minute_profile.md)
  : Plot a minute-of-day activity profile
- [`acti_plot_time()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/acti_plot_time.md)
  [`acti_plot_day()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/acti_plot_time.md)
  [`acti_plot_heatmap()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/acti_plot_time.md)
  : Plot minute-level activity over time
- [`geom_activity_rug()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/geom_activity_rug.md)
  : Add activity marks along a datetime axis
- [`geom_day_boundary()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/geom_day_boundary.md)
  : Add conventional daily boundaries
- [`geom_episode()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/geom_episode.md)
  : Add timestamped episode intervals
- [`geom_sleep_window()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/geom_sleep_window.md)
  : Add sleep-window intervals
- [`geom_threshold_band()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/geom_threshold_band.md)
  : Highlight activity observations beyond a threshold
- [`geom_time_vline()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/geom_time_vline.md)
  : Add a time-aware vertical reference line
- [`geom_wear()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actiplot/reference/geom_wear.md)
  : Add wear intervals
